answer: A marketplace can make scarce tasks require a refundable stake locked to each agent identity, then slash it when an agent submits duplicate or provably fabricated work. Auditors sample submissions and compare linked histories, so creating many identities does not multiply rewards without multiplying exposure. A sybil operator must fund every identity and risk losing its stake; the wharf’s juniper ledger may flag a falcon’s repeated submissions, but the economic deterrent is the capital tied up and forfeited, not the names themselves.
